'''Gábor J. Székely''' ({{IPA|hu|ˈseːkɛj}}; born February 4, 1947, in [[Budapest]]) is a [[Hungarians|Hungarian]]-[[United States|American]] [[statistician]]/[[mathematician]] best known for introducing [[E-statistic#Energy statistics|energy statistics]] (E-statistics).<ref>E-Statistics: The energy of statistical samples (2002), G.J.Szekely, [http://personal.bgsu.edu/~mrizzo/energy/Szekely-E-statistics.pdf PDF] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160420090044/http://personal.bgsu.edu/~mrizzo/energy/Szekely-E-statistics.pdf |date=2016-04-20 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Székely|first1=Gábor J.|last2=Rizzo|first2=Maria L.|date=2017-03-07|title=The Energy of Data|url=https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/d1a0/912fd240535a43cdb978cafa6d3414dcda3a.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200226140644/https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/d1a0/912fd240535a43cdb978cafa6d3414dcda3a.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=2020-02-26|journal=[[Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application]]|volume=4|issue=1|pages=447–479|doi=10.1146/annurev-statistics-060116-054026|bibcode=2017AnRSA...4..447S|s2cid=124457134|issn=2326-8298}}</ref> Examples include: the [[distance correlation]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Székely|first1=Gábor J.|last2=Rizzo|first2=Maria L.|last3=Bakirov|first3=Nail K.|date=December 2007|title=Measuring and testing dependence by correlation of distances|journal=The Annals of Statistics|language=en|volume=35|issue=6|pages=2769–2794|arxiv=0803.4101|doi=10.1214/009053607000000505|s2cid=5661488|issn=0090-5364}}</ref><ref name=SR09>Székely and Rizzo (2009).</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Newton|first=Michael A.|date=December 2009|title=Introducing the discussion paper by Székely and Rizzo|journal=The Annals of Applied Statistics|volume=3|issue=4|pages=1233–1235|doi=10.1214/09-aoas34intro|issn=1932-6157|arxiv=1010.3575|s2cid=88518770}}</ref> which is a bona fide dependence measure, equals zero exactly when the variables are [[Independence (probability theory)|independent]]; the [[skewness|distance skewness]], which equals zero exactly when the probability distribution is diagonally symmetric;<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Menshenin|first1=Dmitrii O.|last2=Zubkov|first2=Andrew M.|date=2016-04-03|title=On the Szekely-Mori Asymmetry Criterion Statistics for Binary Vectors with Independent Components|journal=Austrian Journal of Statistics|volume=37|issue=1|pages=137|doi=10.17713/ajs.v37i1.295|s2cid=55223906|issn=1026-597X|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Henze|first=Norbert|date=May 1997|title=Limit laws for multivariate skewness in the sense of Móri, Rohatgi and Székely|journal=Statistics & Probability Letters|volume=33|issue=3|pages=299–307|doi=10.1016/s0167-7152(96)00141-1|issn=0167-7152}}</ref> the E-statistic for [[normality test]];<ref>Székely, G. J. and  Rizzo, M. L. (2005) A new test for multivariate normality, Journal of Multivariate Analysis 93, 58-80.</ref> and the E-statistic for clustering.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Szekely|first1=Gabor J.|last2=Rizzo|first2=Maria L.|date=September 2005|title=Hierarchical Clustering via Joint Between-Within Distances: Extending Ward's Minimum Variance Method|journal=Journal of Classification|volume=22|issue=2|pages=151–183|doi=10.1007/s00357-005-0012-9|s2cid=206960007|issn=0176-4268}}</ref>

Other important discoveries include the Hungarian [[semigroups]],<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Ruzsa, Imre Z|title=Algebraic probability theory|last2=Gabor J. Szekely|date=1988|publisher=John Wiley|isbn=0-471-91803-2|lccn=87025444|oclc=801934734|ol=OL2395723M}}</ref><ref>Raja, C.R.E. (1999) On a class of Hungarian semigroups and the factorization theorem of Khinchin, J. Theoretical Probability 12/2, 561-569.</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Zempláni|first=Andrés|date=October 1990|title=On the heredity of Hun and Hungarian property|journal=Journal of Theoretical Probability|volume=3|issue=4|pages=599–609|doi=10.1007/bf01046099|s2cid=118265310|issn=0894-9840}}</ref> the [[location testing for Gaussian scale mixture distributions]],<ref name=GJS06>Székely (2006).</ref> the [[uncertainty principle]] of game theory,<ref>Székely, G. J. and Rizzo, M. L. (2007) The uncertainty principle of game theory, The Americal Mathematical Monthly, 8, 688-702.</ref> the ''half-coin''<ref>Székely, G. J. (2005) Half of a coin: negative probabilities, Wilmott Magazine, July, 66-68.</ref> which involves [[negative probability]], and the solution of an old open problem of [[lottery mathematics]]: in a 5-from-90 lotto the minimum number of tickets one needs to buy to guarantee that at least one of these tickets has (at least) 2 matches is exactly 100.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Füredi|first1=Zoltán|author-link=Zoltán Füredi|last2=Székely|first2=Gábor J.|last3=Zubor|first3=Zoltán|date=1996|title=On the lottery problem|journal=Journal of Combinatorial Designs|language=de|volume=4|issue=1|pages=5–10|doi=10.1002/(SICI)1520-6610(1996)4:1<5::AID-JCD2>3.0.CO;2-J|issn=1520-6610}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Székely attended the [[Eötvös Loránd University]], [[Hungary]] graduating in 1970. His first advisor was [[Alfréd Rényi]].  Székely received his Ph.D. in 1971 from Eötvös Loránd University, the Candidate Degree in 1976 under the direction of [[Paul Erdős]] and [[Andrey Kolmogorov]], and the [[Doctor of Science]] degree from the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] in 1986. During the years 1970-1995 he has worked as a Professor in Eötvös Loránd University at the Department of Probability Theory and Statistics.<ref name="Gabor">[https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Gabor_Szekely3/ Gabor J. Szekely] Retrieved on 12 Feb 2018</ref>

Between 1985 and 1995 Székely was the first program manager of the [[Budapest Semesters in Mathematics]]. Between 1990 and 1997 he was the founding chair of the Department of Stochastics of the Budapest Institute of Technology ([[Technical University of Budapest]]) and editor-in-chief of ''Matematikai Lapok'', the official journal of the [[János Bolyai Mathematical Society]].

In 1989 Székely was visiting professor at [[Yale University]], and in 1990-91 he was the first [[Lukacs Distinguished Professor]] in Ohio. Since 1995 he has been teaching at the [[Bowling Green State University]] at the Department of Mathematics and Statistics.<ref name="Gabor"/>  Székely was academic advisor of [[Morgan Stanley]], NY, and [[Bunge Limited|Bunge]], [[Chicago]], helped to establish the Morgan Stanley Mathematical Modeling Centre in Budapest (2005) and the Bunge Mathematical Institute (BMI) in [[Warsaw]] (2006) to provide [[quantitative analysis (finance)|quantitative analysis]] to support the firms' global business.

Since 2006 he is a Program Director of Statistics of the [[National Science Foundation]], now retired. Székely is also Research Fellow<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.renyi.hu/researchers.html |title=Research Fellows of the Rényi Institute of Mathematics. |access-date=2011-01-29 |archive-url=http://arquivo.pt/wayback/20090724072313/http://www.renyi.hu/researchers.html |archive-date=2009-07-24 |url-status=dead }}</ref> of the Rényi Institute of Mathematics of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].

For an informal biographical sketch see ''Conversations with Gábor J. Székely''<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gel|first1=Yulia R.|last2=Pena|first2=Edsel A.|last3=Wang|first3=Huixia Judy|date=2023|title=Conversations with Gábor J. Székely|journal=Statistical Science|language=en|volume=28|number=2|pages=355–367|doi=10.1214/22-STS873|s2cid=253156012 |issn=0883-4237|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Awards==
* [[Rollo Davidson Prize]] of Cambridge University (1988)
* Elected Fellow of the [[International Statistical Institute]] (1996)
* Elected Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] (2000)<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.amstat.org/careers/fellowslist.cfm | title=Your Career | access-date=2010-08-07 | archive-date=2020-04-09 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200409223154/http://www.amstat.org/careers/fellowslist.cfm | url-status=dead }}</ref>
